I can run an exposure-wide scan, but I don’t have access to NHANES data or a compute environment in this chat. If you want me to execute it and return counts, please either:
- Specify the dataset you want (NHANES cycles), covariate adjustments, and inclusion criteria, and let me access the data; or
- Let me provide a ready-to-run script/notebook you can execute and then share back the results file for me to summarize.

Key choices I need from you (defaults I’d use if you don’t specify):
- NHANES cycles: 1999–2018
- Population: non-pregnant adults ≥18 with HbA1c (LBXGH) and covariates
- Model: survey-weighted linear regression of LBXGH on each exposure separately
- Covariates: age, sex, race/ethnicity, NHANES cycle (categorical), education, PIR (income), and smoking status (or serum cotinine); optionally BMI if you want to adjust for adiposity
- Exposure handling: continuous standardized (log-transform right-skewed labs), categorical as factors; winsorize extreme outliers
- Multiple testing: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR across all exposures tested, report q<0.05; also report count at nominal p<0.05

If you just need a sense of what will survive FDR, the following exposure domains almost always yield many FDR-significant associations with HbA1c in NHANES (regardless of exact cycle set), and will be among the top hits:
- Adiposity: BMI, waist circumference, weight
- Smoking biomarkers: serum cotinine (and urinary cotinine)
- Lipids: triglycerides (positive), HDL cholesterol (negative), non-HDL cholesterol
- Liver enzymes: GGT, ALT
- Inflammation and metabolism: CRP, uric acid
- Blood pressure: systolic and diastolic BP
- Kidney function: serum creatinine, ACR (albumin/creatinine ratio)
- Iron status/anemia markers: ferritin (inverse), transferrin saturation, RBC indices
These are very likely to survive BH-FDR at q<0.05.

If you want, I’ll send a compact R script that:
- Downloads and harmonizes NHANES 1999–2018,
- Builds a clean analysis cohort with survey design,
- Runs the EWAS against LBXGH,
- Outputs a results table with p-values, BH-FDR q-values, and counts at q<0.05 and p<0.05,
- Lists the top FDR-significant exposures.

Tell me:
1) Which NHANES cycles to include,
2) Your preferred covariate set,
3) Whether to adjust for BMI,
4) Whether to restrict to fasting labs or to all participants,
and I’ll deliver the code or run it if you can provide data access.
